title: Bounded cosimplicial replacements in a combinatorial model category
statement: Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence, cofibrant-object and Reedy terminology of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A model category is combinatorial when its underlying category is locally presentable and its two weak factorization systems have small generating sets. An object is $\lambda$-presentable if its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits; $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone. Locally $\lambda$-presentable means generated under these colimits by a small family of $\lambda$-presentable objects. A cosimplicial resolution means a Reedy cofibrant functor $A^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ whose structure maps are weak equivalences. Its canonical augmentation to $\operatorname{const}(A^0)$ is induced by the unique maps $[n]\to[0]$. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial. There exist an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$, a small full representative category $B$ of the $\lambda$-presentable objects, and a functorial cofibrant replacement $Q\to\mathrm{id}$ such that $\mathcal M$ is locally $\lambda$-presentable, $\lambda$-filtered colimits preserve objectwise weak equivalences, and $Q$ preserves $\lambda$-presentable objects. Put $C=B^{\mathrm{cof}}$. Let $E$ be a small model of the full category of cosimplicial objects with cofibrant $\lambda$-presentable terms. There is a functor $R:E\to E$ with a natural objectwise weak equivalence $\eta_A:RA\to A$ such that $RA$ is Reedy cofibrant, $(RA)^0=A^0$, and $\eta_A^0=1_{A^0}$. Constant diagrams on $C$ are objects of $E$. All representative choices and transports can be fixed functorially, keeping the specified degree-zero identifications. The full subcategory $D\subset E$ of cosimplicial resolutions is small; $R$ carries every object of $D$, and every constant diagram on an object of $C$, into $D$. No simplicial enrichment of $\mathcal M$ is required.
